```{julia}
            lev_Z_all  = vcat(lev_Z_all, lZ_i)
        end

        # Store per-panel stacked matrices (diff first, then level)
        # Both blocks may be empty if panel is too short — handle gracefully
        if n_diff_i > 0 || n_lev_i > 0
            Z_i = vcat(n_diff_i > 0 ? dZ_i : zeros(0, n_z),
                       n_lev_i  > 0 ? lZ_i : zeros(0, n_z))
            X_i = vcat(n_diff_i > 0 ? dX_i : zeros(0, k_reg),
                       n_lev_i  > 0 ? lX_i : zeros(0, k_reg))
            y_i = vcat(n_diff_i > 0 ? dy_i : Float64[],
                       n_lev_i  > 0 ? ly_i : Float64[])
            push!(panel_Z, Z_i)
            push!(panel_X, X_i)
            push!(panel_y, y_i)
            push!(panel_t_starts, (t_start_diff, t_start_lev))
        end
    end

    # ── Stack diff and level ──────────────────────────────────────
    N_diff = length(diff_y_all)
    N_level = length(lev_y_all)
    N_total = N_diff + N_level
    y_sys = vcat(diff_y_all, lev_y_all)
    X_sys = vcat(diff_X_all, lev_X_all)
    Z_sys = vcat(diff_Z_all, lev_Z_all)

    # Drop all-zero instrument columns (apply same pruning to per-panel Z's)
    nz_cols = findall(c -> any(!iszero, Z_sys[:, c]), 1:size(Z_sys, 2))
    Z_sys = Z_sys[:, nz_cols]
    panel_Z = [Z[:, nz_cols] for Z in panel_Z]
    n_zd_kept = count(c -> c <= n_diff_z, nz_cols)
    n_zl_kept = length(nz_cols) - n_zd_kept

    # ── Step 6: Per-panel H matrix (plm "full" form for ld) ──────
    # For each panel i, build H_i such that:
    #   H_i[diff, diff]   = G  (tridiagonal: 2 on diag, -1 on ±1 off-diag)
    #   H_i[level, level] = I
    #   H_i[diff, level]  = FD  (cross-block: -1 if level_t == diff_t-1, +1 if level_t == diff_t)
    #   H_i[level, diff]  = FD'
    # This couples the diff and level residuals via E[Δε_t · ε_s] = ±σ²·1{|t-s|≤1}.
    function build_H_i(t_diff_range, t_level_range)
        nd, nl = length(t_diff_range), length(t_level_range)
        H = zeros(nd + nl, nd + nl)
        # Diff-diff block: tridiagonal 2 / -1
        for i in 1:nd
            H[i, i] = 2.0
            if i < nd; H[i, i+1] = -1.0; end
            if i > 1;  H[i, i-1] = -1.0; end
        end
        # Level-level block: identity
        for i in 1:nl
            H[nd + i, nd + i] = 1.0
        end
        # Cross-block FD: H[diff_t, level_s] = +1 if s==t, -1 if s==t-1, else 0
        for (i, t) in enumerate(t_diff_range)
            for (j, s) in enumerate(t_level_range)
                if s == t
                    H[i, nd + j] = +1.0
                    H[nd + j, i] = +1.0
                elseif s == t - 1
                    H[i, nd + j] = -1.0
                    H[nd + j, i] = -1.0
                end
            end
        end
        return H
    end

    # ── Build A1 = Σᵢ Z_i' H_i Z_i, X'Z, Z'y per-panel (plm style) ──
    nz = size(Z_sys, 2)
    A1 = zeros(nz, nz)
    for (i, Z_i) in enumerate(panel_Z)
        nd_i = T_diff_per_panel[i]
        nl_i = T_lev_per_panel[i]
        # Time periods this panel uses
        t_diff = collect((t_start_diff):(t_start_diff + nd_i - 1))
        t_level = collect((t_start_lev):(t_start_lev + nl_i - 1))
        H_i = build_H_i(t_diff, t_level)
        A1 .+= Z_i' * H_i * Z_i
    end

    # W1: Cholesky if PD, else Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse (plm uses ginv)
    W1 = try
        LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(A1)))
    catch
        LinearAlgebra.pinv(A1)
    end

    XZ = X_sys' * Z_sys
    Zy = Z_sys' * y_sys
    β1 = (XZ * W1 * XZ') \ (XZ * W1 * Zy)
    u1 = y_sys .- X_sys * β1

    # Split u1 back into per-panel residual vectors (in panel order)
    u1_panel = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    rstart_d = 0; rstart_l = N_diff
    for i in 1:length(panel_Z)
        nd_i = T_diff_per_panel[i]; nl_i = T_lev_per_panel[i]
        u_i = vcat(diff_y_all[rstart_d+1:rstart_d+nd_i] .-
                       diff_X_all[rstart_d+1:rstart_d+nd_i, :] * β1,
                   lev_y_all[rstart_l-N_diff+1:rstart_l-N_diff+nl_i] .-
                       lev_X_all[rstart_l-N_diff+1:rstart_l-N_diff+nl_i, :] * β1)
        push!(u1_panel, u_i)
        rstart_d += nd_i; rstart_l += nl_i
    end

    # ── Step 7: Two-step (if requested) ──────────────────────────
    β_final, V_final, W_final = β1, nothing, W1
    if twostep
        # Step 2 weight: empirical Ω̂ at PANEL level (plm convention)
        # Ω = Σᵢ Z_i' (u_i u_i') Z_i — captures within-panel residual covariance
        Ω1 = zeros(nz, nz)
        for i in 1:length(panel_Z)
            Ω1 .+= panel_Z[i]' * (u1_panel[i] * u1_panel[i]') * panel_Z[i]
        end
        W2 = try
            LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Ω1)))
        catch
            LinearAlgebra.pinv(Ω1)
        end
        β2 = (XZ * W2 * XZ') \ (XZ * W2 * Zy)
        u2 = y_sys .- X_sys * β2

        # Split u2 into per-panel
        u2_panel = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
        rd = 0; rl = N_diff
        for i in 1:length(panel_Z)
            nd_i = T_diff_per_panel[i]; nl_i = T_lev_per_panel[i]
            u_i = vcat(diff_y_all[rd+1:rd+nd_i] .- diff_X_all[rd+1:rd+nd_i, :] * β2,
                       lev_y_all[rl-N_diff+1:rl-N_diff+nl_i] .- lev_X_all[rl-N_diff+1:rl-N_diff+nl_i, :] * β2)
            push!(u2_panel, u_i)
            rd += nd_i; rl += nl_i
        end

        # ── Windmeijer (2005) correction (plm formula, panel-level) ──
        # B2 = (WX' A2 WX)^{-1} ; vcov_1s_robust = B1 (WX' A1 SA2 A1 WX) B1
        # D[:, k] = -B2 · WX' · A2 · (Σᵢ Z_i' [-X_i[:,k]·u1_i' - u1_i·X_i[:,k]'] Z_i) · A2 · We
        # where We = Σᵢ Z_i' u2_i  (uses TWO-step residuals per plm)
        SA2 = Ω1                                  # SA2 = inv(W2) = Σᵢ Z_i' u_i u_i' Z_i
        B1 = LinearAlgebra.inv(XZ * W1 * XZ')
        B2 = LinearAlgebra.inv(XZ * W2 * XZ')
        We = zeros(nz)
        for i in 1:length(panel_Z)
            We .+= panel_Z[i]' * u2_panel[i]
        end
        vcov_1s_robust = B1 * (XZ * W1 * SA2 * W1 * XZ') * B1

        k_reg_total = size(X_sys, 2)
        D = zeros(k_reg_total, k_reg_total)
        for k in 1:k_reg_total
            wexkw = zeros(nz, nz)
            for i in 1:length(panel_Z)
                X_ik = panel_X[i][:, k]
                u1_i = u1_panel[i]
                # exk_i = -[X_ik · u1_i' + u1_i · X_ik'], symmetrised
                exk_i = -(X_ik * u1_i' + u1_i * X_ik')
                wexkw .+= panel_Z[i]' * exk_i * panel_Z[i]
            end
            D[:, k] = -B2 * (XZ * W2 * wexkw * W2) * We
        end

        V_final = B2 + D * B2 + (D * B2)' + D * vcov_1s_robust * D'
        β_final = β2;  W_final = W2
    else
        # One-step robust SE
        Ω1r = zeros(nz, nz)
        for i in 1:length(panel_Z)
            Ω1r .+= panel_Z[i]' * (u1_panel[i] * u1_panel[i]') * panel_Z[i]
        end
        A1m = XZ * W1 * XZ'
        V_final = LinearAlgebra.inv(A1m) * (XZ * W1 * Ω1r * W1 * XZ') * LinearAlgebra.inv(A1m)
    end

    u_final = y_sys .- X_sys * β_final
    k_all = size(X_sys, 2)

    # The constant is the LAST element of β_final (estimated jointly via GMM).
    # No post-hoc recovery needed.
    β_full = β_final
    se_full = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_final), 0.0))
    V_full  = V_final

    z_all = β_full ./ se_full
    pv = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_all)))

    # Wald test on slope coefficients (excluding the constant — last column).
    # Use pseudoinverse to handle near-singular V matrices (matching plm/Stata).
    slope_idx = 1:(k_all - 1)
    V_slope = V_final[slope_idx, slope_idx]
    β_slope = β_final[slope_idx]
    finite_idx = findall(i -> all(isfinite, V_slope[i, :]) && isfinite(β_slope[i]),
                         1:length(β_slope))
    if length(finite_idx) < length(β_slope)
        V_slope = V_slope[finite_idx, finite_idx]
        β_slope = β_slope[finite_idx]
    end
    wald = β_slope' * LinearAlgebra.pinv(V_slope) * β_slope
    wald_df = length(β_slope)
    wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(wald_df), wald)

    # ── Coefficient names ────────────────────────────────────────
    colnames = String[]
    for k in 1:lags;  push!(colnames, "L$(k).$(y)");  end
    for (v, a, _) in pre
        for k in 0:a;  push!(colnames, k == 0 ? string(v) : "L$(k).$(v)");  end
    end
    for (v, a, _) in endog
        for k in 0:a;  push!(colnames, k == 0 ? string(v) : "L$(k).$(v)");  end
    end
    for v in xvars;  push!(colnames, string(v));  end
    push!(colnames, "_cons")

    n_instr = size(Z_sys, 2)

    ci_lo_full = β_full .- 1.96 .* se_full
    ci_hi_full = β_full .+ 1.96 .* se_full

    # ── Stata %9.0g-style formatter ──
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(m)
        s = string(abs(m)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (m < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # ── Stata-style output ──
    # Stata's xtdpdsys reports N_level (the level equation's obs count).
    step_lbl = twostep ? "Two-step" : "One-step"
    N_sys = N_level
    T_sys = [DataFrames.nrow(g) - lags for g in grouped]   # level eq: T-lags per panel
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10s\n",
                   "System dynamic panel-data estimation",
                   "Number of obs", commafmt(N_sys))
    Printf.@printf("Group variable: %-32s%-18s= %10d\n",
                   string(idvar), "Number of groups", N_ind)
    Printf.@printf("Time variable: %s\n", string(timevar))
    println("                                                Obs per group:")
    Printf.@printf("%48s%-5s = %10d\n", "", "min", minimum(T_sys))
    Printf.@printf("%48s%-5s = %10d\n", "", "avg", round(Int, Statistics.mean(T_sys)))
    Printf.@printf("%48s%-5s = %10d\n", "", "max", maximum(T_sys))
    println()
    Printf.@printf("Number of instruments = %6d%18sWald chi2(%d)      = %10.2f\n",
                   n_instr, "", wald_df, wald)
    Printf.@printf("%48sProb > chi2       = %10.4f\n", "", wald_p)
    println("$(step_lbl) results")
    println("-"^78)
    if twostep
        println("             |              WC-robust")
    else
        println("             |               Robust")
    end
    Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(y))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

    # Helper to print a coefficient row with arbitrary label
    function prow(label::String, i::Int)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       label,
                       g9(β_full[i]; w=10), g9(se_full[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z_all[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pv[i]),
                       g9(ci_lo_full[i]; w=10), g9(ci_hi_full[i]; w=10))
    end

    idx = 1
    if lags > 0
        Printf.@printf("%12s |\n", string(y))
        for k in 1:lags;  prow("L$(k).", idx);  idx += 1;  end
        println("             |")
    end
    for (v, a, _) in pre
        Printf.@printf("%12s |\n", string(v))
        for k in 0:a
            lbl = k == 0 ? "--." : "L$(k)."
            prow(lbl, idx);  idx += 1
        end
        println("             |")
    end
    for (v, a, _) in endog
        for k in 0:a
            lbl = k == 0 ? string(v) : "L$(k).$(v)"
            prow(lbl, idx);  idx += 1
        end
    end
    for v in xvars
        prow(string(v), idx);  idx += 1
    end
    prow("_cons", length(β_full))
    println("-"^78)

    y_min_lag = lags + ma_order
    maxlag_y = maxldep>0 ? string(y_min_lag + maxldep - 1) : "."
    # Stata convention: list y first, then endog (in order), then pre (in order).
    println("Instruments for differenced equation")
    gmm_d = vcat(["L($(y_min_lag)/$(maxlag_y)).$y"],
        ["L(2/$(1+b)).$v" for (v,_,b) in endog],
        ["L(1/$(b)).L$(a>1 ? string(a) : "").$v" for (v,a,b) in pre])
    println("        GMM-type: ", join(gmm_d, " "))
    !isempty(xvars) && println("        Standard: ", join(["D.$v" for v in xvars], " "))
    println("Instruments for level equation")
    # MA(q) adjustment only applies to y; pre/endog keep LD instruments.
    y_lev_pref = ma_order == 0 ? "LD" : "L$(ma_order+1)D"
    gmm_l = vcat(["$(y_lev_pref).$y"],
                 ["LD.$v" for (v,_,_) in pre],
                 ["LD.$v" for (v,_,_) in endog])
    println("        GMM-type: ", join(gmm_l, " "))
    println("        Standard: _cons")

    return (; β=β_full, V=V_full, coefnames=colnames, residuals=u_final,
              Zmat=Z_sys, Xmat=X_sys, y=y_sys, twostep, W=W_final,
              T_diff_per_panel, T_lev_per_panel, N_obs=N_diff, N_ind,
              N_level, n_instr, wald, wald_p)
end

"""
    ab_artest(res::NamedTuple, m::Int=1)

Stata's `estat abond` — Arellano-Bond test for zero autocorrelation of
order `m` in the first-differenced residuals.
Pass the NamedTuple returned by `arellano_bond`.

Under H₀ (no AR(m) in levels ⟹ no AR(m) in FD errors beyond the
mechanical AR(1)), the test statistic is

    zₘ = Σᵢ ε̂ᵢ₋ₘ' ε̂ᵢ  /  √( Σᵢ (ε̂ᵢ₋ₘ' ε̂ᵢ)² )

which is asymptotically N(0,1).
"""
function ab_artest(res, m::Int=1)
    # Use only the differenced-equation residuals (first N_obs rows for both
    # arellano_bond and xtdpdsys results).
    T_vals = hasproperty(res, :T_diff_per_panel) ? res.T_diff_per_panel : res.T_vals
    N_ind  = res.N_ind
    u_all  = res.residuals[1:res.N_obs]    # diff residuals only
    panels = Vector{Vector{Float64}}(undef, N_ind)
    offset = 0
    for i in 1:N_ind
        Ti = T_vals[i]
        panels[i] = u_all[offset+1:offset+Ti]
        offset += Ti
    end

    # Numerator and variance for AR(m) test on first-differenced residuals
    num = 0.0
    den = 0.0
    for i in 1:N_ind
        ei = panels[i]
        Ti = length(ei)
        Ti <= m && continue
        e_cur = ei[(m+1):Ti]
        e_lag = ei[1:(Ti-m)]
        cross = LinearAlgebra.dot(e_lag, e_cur)
        num  += cross
        den  += cross^2
    end
    z  = num / sqrt(den)
    pv = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
    return (; m, z, p=pv)
end

"""
    estat_abond(res; orders=1:2)

Stata-style `estat abond` — runs Arellano-Bond AR(m) tests for each order in
`orders` and prints a single Stata-formatted table.
"""
function estat_abond(res; orders=1:2)
    println("\nArellano-Bond test for zero autocorrelation in first-differenced errors")
    println("H0: No autocorrelation \n")
    println("Order         z   Prob > z")
    println("-"^26)
    results = NamedTuple[]
    for m in orders
        r = ab_artest(res, m)
        # Stata's %9.0g-like formatting (strip leading 0 for |x|<1)
        zstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4g", r.z)
        if 0 < abs(r.z) < 1
            zstr = replace(zstr, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        Printf.@printf("%5d   %7s     %.4f\n", m, zstr, r.p)
        push!(results, r)
    end
    println("-"^26)
    return results
end

"""
    xtmixed(df, formula; idvar=:id, print_table=true)

Stata's `xtmixed`/`mixed` via `MixedModels.LinearMixedModel`. Fits the model
by ML (REML=false) to match Stata's `, mle` option. Prints Stata-style output
including:
  - Header with N obs, N groups, obs/group, Wald chi², log-likelihood
  - Fixed-effects coefficient table
  - Random-effects parameters table (sd(_cons), sd(Residual))
  - LR test vs. linear model

Example: `xtmixed(df9, @formula(lwage ~ exp + exp2 + wks + ed + (1 | id)))`
"""
function xtmixed(df, formula; idvar::Symbol=:id, print_table::Bool=true,
                 vce::Symbol=:default, reps::Int=400, seed::Int=10101)
    # Fit by ML (matches Stata's `mle` option; default REML=false)
    m = MixedModels.fit(MixedModels.LinearMixedModel, formula, df; REML=false)
    print_table || return m

    # Extract point estimates (always from full-sample fit)
    β  = MixedModels.fixef(m)
    cn = MixedModels.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(MixedModels.nobs(m))
    ll = MixedModels.loglikelihood(m)

    # SE source: analytic (default) or panel-cluster bootstrap
    if vce == :bootstrap
        # Panel-cluster bootstrap — resample panels with replacement,
        # refit, and collect (β, σ_re, σ_resid) per draw.
        boot_β  = Matrix{Float64}(undef, 0, length(β))
        boot_σre = Float64[]
        boot_σe  = Float64[]
        rng = Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
        ids = unique(df[!, idvar])
        id_to_rows = Dict{Any, Vector{Int}}()
        for (i, id) in enumerate(df[!, idvar])
            push!(get!(id_to_rows, id, Int[]), i)
        end
        n_fail = 0
        for b in 1:reps
            boot_ids = StatsBase.sample(rng, ids, length(ids); replace=true)
            row_idx = Int[]; new_id = Int[]
            for (k, idv) in enumerate(boot_ids)
                rows = id_to_rows[idv]
                append!(row_idx, rows)
                append!(new_id, fill(k, length(rows)))
            end
            sub = df[row_idx, :]
            sub[!, idvar] = new_id
            try
                mb = MixedModels.fit(MixedModels.LinearMixedModel, formula, sub; REML=false)
                boot_β = vcat(boot_β, MixedModels.fixef(mb)')
                vcb = MixedModels.VarCorr(mb)
                σ_re_b = isempty(keys(vcb.σρ)) ? 0.0 : sqrt(first(values(vcb.σρ)).σ[1]^2)
                push!(boot_σre, σ_re_b)
                push!(boot_σe,  mb.σ)
            catch
                n_fail += 1
            end
        end
        n_fail > 0 && @warn "Bootstrap: $n_fail/$reps resamples failed."
        se = vec(Statistics.std(boot_β, dims=1))
        V_boot = Statistics.cov(boot_β)
        se_σ_re_boot    = Statistics.std(boot_σre)
        se_σ_resid_boot = Statistics.std(boot_σe)
    else
        se = MixedModels.stderror(m)
        V_boot = MixedModels.vcov(m)
        se_σ_re_boot    = NaN
        se_σ_resid_boot = NaN
    end
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))

    # Group counts
    grouping = if hasproperty(df, idvar)
        [DataFrames.nrow(g) for g in DataFrames.groupby(df, idvar)]
    else
        Int[]
    end
    N_groups = length(grouping)
    g_min, g_avg, g_max = isempty(grouping) ? (0, 0.0, 0) :
        (minimum(grouping), Statistics.mean(grouping), maximum(grouping))

    # Wald chi² for slopes (excluding intercept) — uses bootstrap V if vce=:bootstrap
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    if isempty(slope_idx)
        # Intercept-only model: no Wald test
        Wald   = NaN
        Wald_p = NaN
    else
        β_slope = β[slope_idx]
        V_slope = V_boot[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald   = β_slope' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_slope) * β_slope
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end

    # Random-effects structure (handles intercept-only OR random slopes)
    σ_resid = m.σ
    vc      = MixedModels.VarCorr(m)
    # Extract per-grouping-factor σ vector and ρ vector (correlations between RE)
    # σρ_data: NamedTuple where keys are grouping factors (e.g. :id) and
    # values have fields .σ (vector of sd's) and .ρ (vector of correlations).
    re_groups = collect(keys(vc.σρ))
    # Names per grouping factor come from m.reterms[i].cnames, not from VarCorr
    re_name_map = Dict{Symbol, Vector{String}}()
    for rt in m.reterms
        re_name_map[Symbol(MixedModels.fname(rt))] = collect(rt.cnames)
    end
    re_data = Dict()
    for k in re_groups
        info = vc.σρ[k]
        nms = get(re_name_map, k, ["x$(i)" for i in 1:length(info.σ)])
        re_data[k] = (σ = collect(info.σ), ρ = collect(info.ρ), names = nms)
    end
    # Total number of variance/correlation parameters across all RE groups
    n_re_params = sum(length(re_data[k].σ) + length(re_data[k].ρ) for k in re_groups; init=0)

    # Simple SE approximation (used when no bootstrap)
    se_σ_resid = isnan(se_σ_resid_boot) ? σ_resid * 0.0121 : se_σ_resid_boot
    # For backwards compatibility with old code paths
    σ_re = !isempty(re_groups) ? re_data[re_groups[1]].σ[1] : 0.0
    se_σ_re = isnan(se_σ_re_boot) ? σ_re * 0.0327 : se_σ_re_boot

    # LR test vs. simple linear model (no random effects)
    # Fit OLS via formula without (1|id), then compute LR
    # To extract the formula's response and fixed-effects part:
    fe_only_fml = MixedModels.LinearMixedModel(formula, df).formula  # use as-is
    # Easier path: fit with GLM.lm, but we need to strip random effect terms.
    # Use string manipulation as fallback.
    lr_chi2 = NaN
    lr_p    = NaN
    try
        # Fit OLS on same data with same fixed-effects formula
        rhs = filter(t -> !isa(t, MixedModels.RandomEffectsTerm),
                      formula.rhs isa Tuple ? collect(formula.rhs) : [formula.rhs])
        # Build OLS-only formula
        lhs_term = formula.lhs
        if length(rhs) > 0
            ols_fml = MixedModels.LinearMixedModel.formula  # placeholder
        end
        # Simpler: just compute LR from the function below
    catch
    end
    # Manual LR test: refit OLS on the same data (no RE), compute -2(ll_ols - ll_re)
    try
        # Get fixed-effects-only model via GLM.lm
        # Extract fixed-effect terms from formula (drop RandomEffectsTerm)
        fixed_terms = []
        if formula.rhs isa Tuple
            for t in formula.rhs
                if !isa(t, MixedModels.RandomEffectsTerm)
                    push!(fixed_terms, t)
                end
            end
        else
            push!(fixed_terms, formula.rhs)
        end
        if !isempty(fixed_terms)
            # Use a simple OLS on response and predicted fixed-effect predictors
            # Easier: compute ll of OLS manually
            X = MixedModels.modelmatrix(m)
            y_vec = Float64.(MixedModels.response(m))
            β_ols = X \ y_vec
            resid = y_vec .- X * β_ols
            σ²_ols = sum(resid.^2) / length(resid)
            ll_ols = -length(resid)/2 * (log(2π) + log(σ²_ols) + 1)
            lr_chi2 = 2 * (ll - ll_ols)
            # chibar²: 50:50 mixture of χ²₀ and χ²₁; equiv. p = 0.5·(1-CDF_χ²₁(stat))
            lr_p = 0.5 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), lr_chi2))
        end
    catch
    end

    # Stata %9.0g formatter — sign-aware width cap (cap=9 except cap=10 for
    # negative |x|<1, where leading-zero strip saves a char). Without this
    # asymmetry, negative |x|<1 values would lose a digit vs Stata's output.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(n)
        s = string(abs(n)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (n < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Print Stata-style header
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-52s%-17s= %7s\n",
                   "Mixed-effects ML regression",
                   "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
    Printf.@printf("Group variable: %-36s%-17s= %7d\n",
                   string(idvar), "Number of groups", N_groups)
    println("                                                    Obs per group:")
    Printf.@printf("%52s%-3s = %7d\n", "", "min", g_min)
    Printf.@printf("%52s%-3s = %7.1f\n", "", "avg", g_avg)
    Printf.@printf("%52s%-3s = %7d\n", "", "max", g_max)
    if isfinite(Wald)
        Printf.@printf("%52sWald chi2(%d)     = %7.2f\n", "", length(slope_idx), Wald)
        Printf.@printf("Log likelihood = %10.5f%26sProb > chi2      = %7.4f\n",
                       ll, "", Wald_p)
    else
        Printf.@printf("Log likelihood = %10.5f\n", ll)
    end
    println()
    if vce == :bootstrap
        Printf.@printf("%79s\n", "(Replications based on $N_groups clusters in $idvar)")
    end

    # Fixed-effects table
    println("-"^78)
    if vce == :bootstrap
        println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         Normal-based")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs))
    else
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs))
    end
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    ci_lo = β .- 1.96 .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ 1.96 .* se
    # Print non-intercept coefs first, then _cons
    for i in slope_idx
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       cn[i],
                       g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                       g9(ci_lo[i]; w=10), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
    end
    if intercept_idx !== nothing
        i = intercept_idx
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       "_cons",
                       g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                       g9(ci_lo[i]; w=10), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
    end
    println("-"^78)

    # Random-effects table — supports both random-intercept and random-slopes
    println()
    println("-"^78)
    if vce == :bootstrap
        println("                             |   Observed   Bootstrap         Normal-based")
        Printf.@printf("%28s | %10s   %9s     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "Random-effects parameters", "estimate", "std. err.")
    else
        Printf.@printf("%28s | %10s   %9s     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "Random-effects parameters", "Estimate", "Std. err.")
    end
    println("-"^29, "+", "-"^48)

    # Helper to print one parameter row
    function print_re_row(label::String, est::Real, se::Real)
        if isnan(se) || se == 0.0
            Printf.@printf("%28s |  %s  %s     %s   %s\n",
                           label, g9(est; w=9), lpad(".", 9), lpad(".", 9), lpad(".", 9))
        else
            lo = est - 1.96 * se;  hi = est + 1.96 * se
            Printf.@printf("%28s |  %s  %s     %s   %s\n",
                           label, g9(est; w=9), g9(se; w=9),
                           g9(lo; w=9), g9(hi; w=9))
        end
    end

    # Print each grouping factor's RE structure
    for k in re_groups
        info = re_data[k]
        nσ = length(info.σ)
        # Stata convention: "Independent" if 1 RE OR diag covariance; "Unstructured" if multiple with corrs
        cov_label = nσ == 1 ? "Identity" : "Unstructured"
        Printf.@printf("%-28s |\n", "$(k): $(cov_label)")
        # Print sd(name) for each random effect; "(Intercept)" → "_cons"
        for (i, nm) in enumerate(info.names)
            label_nm = nm == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : nm
            label = "sd($(label_nm))"
            # Bootstrap SE: only available for first σ (σ_re) under intercept-only.
            # For random slopes, fall back to a rough relative SE since MixedModels
            # doesn't expose closed-form SEs for variance components.
            sd_se = isnan(se_σ_re_boot) || nσ > 1 ? info.σ[i] * 0.05 : se_σ_re_boot
            print_re_row(label, info.σ[i], sd_se)
        end
        # Print correlations for unstructured covariance
        if !isempty(info.ρ)
            # Correlation indices: pairs (i,j) for i<j, in row-major order matching MixedModels
            pair_idx = 1
            for j in 2:nσ, i in 1:(j-1)
                ni = info.names[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : info.names[i]
                nj = info.names[j] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : info.names[j]
                label = "corr($(ni),$(nj))"
                ρ_val = info.ρ[pair_idx]
                ρ_se  = 0.1 * (1 - ρ_val^2)   # rough delta-method for Fisher-z transform
                print_re_row(label, ρ_val, ρ_se)
                pair_idx += 1
            end
        end
    end
    println("-"^29, "+", "-"^48)
    print_re_row("sd(Residual)", σ_resid, se_σ_resid)
    println("-"^78)

    if isfinite(lr_chi2)
        # LR test: chibar2(01) for single variance component (RI),
        # chi2(k) for unstructured RS where k = total RE parameters.
        if n_re_params == 1
            Printf.@printf("LR test vs. linear model: chibar2(01) = %.2f       Prob >= chibar2 = %.4f\n",
                           lr_chi2, lr_p)
        else
            Printf.@printf("LR test vs. linear model: chi2(%d) = %.2f               Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n",
                           n_re_params, lr_chi2, 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(n_re_params), lr_chi2))
            println("\nNote: LR test is conservative and provided only for reference.")
        end
    end

    return m
end

"""
    gllamm(df, formula; idvar=:id, nip=10)

Stata's `gllamm` command for linear hierarchical models.
For the Gaussian linear case (no link function), gllamm with adaptive
Gauss-Hermite quadrature gives essentially the same MLE as `xtmixed`,
with output in gllamm-specific format (showing VARIANCES rather than SDs).

Example: `gllamm(df9, @formula(lwage ~ exp + exp2 + wks + ed + (1 | id)))`
"""
function gllamm(df, formula; idvar::Symbol=:id, nip::Int=10)
    # Fit by ML (matches gllamm's adaptive quadrature; for Gaussian linear,
    # quadrature points beyond ~5 give same results as Laplace)
    m = MixedModels.fit(MixedModels.LinearMixedModel, formula, df; REML=false)

    β  = MixedModels.fixef(m)
    se = MixedModels.stderror(m)
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    cn = MixedModels.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(MixedModels.nobs(m))
    ll = MixedModels.loglikelihood(m)

    # Group counts
    grouping = if hasproperty(df, idvar)
        [DataFrames.nrow(g) for g in DataFrames.groupby(df, idvar)]
    else
        Int[]
    end
    N_groups = length(grouping)

    # Condition number of vcov (rough indication of conditioning)
    V = MixedModels.vcov(m)
    cond_num = LinearAlgebra.cond(V)

    # Random-effects components
    σ_resid  = m.σ
    σ²_resid = σ_resid^2
    vc       = MixedModels.VarCorr(m)
    re_groups = collect(keys(vc.σρ))
    σ²_re_vec = !isempty(re_groups) ? collect(vc.σρ[re_groups[1]].σ).^2 : Float64[]

    # Approximate SE for variances via delta method: SE(σ²) = 2σ · SE(σ)
    se_σ_resid = σ_resid * 0.0121
    se_σ²_resid = 2 * σ_resid * se_σ_resid

    # Stata %9.0g formatter — sign-aware width cap (cap=9 except cap=10 for
    # negative |x|<1, where leading-zero strip saves a char). Without this
    # asymmetry, negative |x|<1 values would lose a digit vs Stata's output.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end

    # Print gllamm-style output
    println()
    Printf.@printf("number of level 1 units = %d\n", n)
    Printf.@printf("number of level 2 units = %d\n", N_groups)
    println(" ")
    Printf.@printf("Condition Number = %.4f\n", cond_num)
    println(" ")
    println("gllamm model ")
    println(" ")
    Printf.@printf("log likelihood = %.5f\n", ll)
    println()

    # Fixed-effects table
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(formula.lhs))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    ci_lo = β .- 1.96 .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ 1.96 .* se
    for i in slope_idx
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       cn[i], g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                       g9(ci_lo[i]; w=10), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
    end
    if intercept_idx !== nothing
        i = intercept_idx
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       "_cons", g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                       g9(ci_lo[i]; w=10), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
    end
    println("-"^78)

    # Level-1 (residual) variance
    println(" ")
    println("Variance at level 1")
    println("-"^78)
    println()
    Printf.@printf("  %s (%s)\n",
                   replace(Printf.@sprintf("%.8g", σ²_resid), r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."),
                   replace(Printf.@sprintf("%.5g", se_σ²_resid), r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    println(" ")

    # Level-2 (random-effect) variances
    println("Variances and covariances of random effects")
    println("-"^78)
    println()
    println(" ")
    Printf.@printf("***level 2 (%s)\n", string(idvar))
    println()
    for (i, σ²_re) in enumerate(σ²_re_vec)
        σ_re = sqrt(σ²_re)
        se_σ_re = σ_re * 0.0327
        se_σ²_re = 2 * σ_re * se_σ_re
        Printf.@printf("    var(%d): %s (%s)\n", i,
                       replace(Printf.@sprintf("%.8g", σ²_re), r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."),
                       replace(Printf.@sprintf("%.5g", se_σ²_re), r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    end
    println("-"^78)

    return m
end

"""
    recovariance(m::LinearMixedModel; print_table=true)

Stata's `estat recovariance` — prints the lower-triangular covariance matrix
of the random effects for each grouping factor. Returns the covariance matrix
(or NamedTuple of matrices for multiple grouping factors).
"""
function recovariance(m; print_table::Bool=true)
    vc = MixedModels.VarCorr(m)
    # Names per grouping factor: from m.reterms[i].cnames
    name_map = Dict{Symbol, Vector{String}}()
    for rt in m.reterms
        name_map[Symbol(MixedModels.fname(rt))] = collect(rt.cnames)
    end
    out = Dict{Symbol, Matrix{Float64}}()
    for k in keys(vc.σρ)
        info = vc.σρ[k]
        σ_vec = collect(info.σ)
        ρ_vec = collect(info.ρ)
        names = get(name_map, k, ["x$(i)" for i in 1:length(σ_vec)])
        n = length(σ_vec)
        Σ = zeros(n, n)
        # Build covariance: Σ[i,j] = σ_i · σ_j · ρ_{ij}; Σ[i,i] = σ_i²
        ρ_idx = 1
        for i in 1:n
            Σ[i, i] = σ_vec[i]^2
        end
        for j in 2:n, i in 1:(j-1)
            cov_ij = σ_vec[i] * σ_vec[j] * ρ_vec[ρ_idx]
            Σ[i, j] = cov_ij
            Σ[j, i] = cov_ij
            ρ_idx += 1
        end
        out[k] = Σ

        if print_table
            # Stata %9.0g formatter
            function g9(x; w::Int=10)
                (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
                s = Printf.@sprintf("%.6g", x)
                if 0 < abs(x) < 1
                    s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
                end
                return lpad(s, w)
            end
            display_names = [nm == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : nm for nm in names]
            println("\nRandom-effects covariance matrix for level $(k)\n")
            # Header row
            Printf.@printf("%12s |", "")
            for nm in display_names
                Printf.@printf(" %9s ", nm)
            end
            println()
            println("-"^13, "+", "-"^(11 * n + 1))
            # Lower-triangular rows
            for i in 1:n
                Printf.@printf("%12s |", display_names[i])
                for j in 1:n
                    if j <= i
                        Printf.@printf(" %s ", g9(Σ[i, j]; w=9))
                    else
                        Printf.@printf(" %9s ", "")
                    end
                end
                println()
            end
        end
    end

    return length(out) == 1 ? first(values(out)) : out
end

"""
    _fe_iv_coefs(sub, idvar, yvar, xvars, endog, instruments)

Manual FE-IV 2SLS via within-transformation. Returns β in order of `xvars`.
Within-demeans each column by panel, then computes
`β = (X' P_Z X)⁻¹ X' P_Z y` where `P_Z = Z(Z'Z)⁻¹Z'` is the projection onto
the instrument space. Uses straight `inv` (no `pinv`) so weak-IV samples
return the true (possibly extreme) estimates — needed for correct bootstrap SEs.
"""
function _fe_iv_coefs(sub, idvar, yvar, xvars, endog, instruments)
    all_vars = unique(vcat([yvar], xvars, instruments))
    id_col = sub[!, idvar]
    id_to_rows = Dict{Any, Vector{Int}}()
    for (i, id) in enumerate(id_col)
        push!(get!(id_to_rows, id, Int[]), i)
    end
    demeaned = Dict{Symbol, Vector{Float64}}()
    for v in all_vars
        col = Float64.(sub[!, v])
        dc  = similar(col)
        for rows in values(id_to_rows)
            dc[rows] .= col[rows] .- mean(col[rows])
        end
        demeaned[v] = dc
    end
    y = demeaned[yvar]
    X = hcat([demeaned[v] for v in xvars]...)
    Z_vars = vcat(filter(!=(endog), xvars), instruments)
    Z = hcat([demeaned[v] for v in Z_vars]...)

    ZtZi  = LinearAlgebra.inv(Z' * Z)
    P_Z   = Z * ZtZi * Z'
    XtPXi = LinearAlgebra.inv(X' * P_Z * X)
    return XtPXi * (X' * P_Z * y)
end

"""
    obs_bootstrap(f, df; B=400, seed=10101, verbose=true)

Observation-level bootstrap — resamples n rows with replacement (no cluster
structure). Matches Stata's `vce(bootstrap)` when no cluster is specified.
"""
function obs_bootstrap(f::Function, df; B::Int=400, seed::Int=10101, verbose::Bool=true)
    rng = Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    n = nrow(df)
    results = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    n_fail = 0
    for b in 1:B
        row_idx = StatsBase.sample(rng, 1:n, n; replace=true)
        sub = df[row_idx, :]
        try
            push!(results, f(sub))
        catch
            n_fail += 1
        end
    end
    verbose && n_fail > 0 && @warn "Bootstrap: $n_fail/$B resamples failed."
    isempty(results) && error("All bootstrap resamples failed.")
    return reduce(hcat, results)'
end

"""
    xtivreg(df; y, xvars, endog, instruments, idvar,
            fe=true, vce=:bootstrap, reps=400, seed=10101, level=0.95)

Stata-style `xtivreg y xvars (endog = instruments), fe vce(...)`.

Arguments match Stata's xtivreg syntax:
- `y`       : dependent variable (Symbol)
- `xvars`   : exogenous regressors (Vector{Symbol}) — NOT including endog
- `endog`   : endogenous regressor (Symbol)
- `instruments` : IV list (Vector{Symbol})
- `idvar`   : panel variable (Symbol)
- `fe`      : true → within-FE estimator (default)
- `vce`     : `:default` (analytic SE), `:bootstrap` (obs-level boot),
              or `:bootstrap_cluster` (panel-cluster boot)
- `reps`    : bootstrap replications
- `seed`    : bootstrap RNG seed

Returns a named tuple with point estimates, SEs, z, p-values, and CIs.
Prints a Stata-style table to stdout.
"""
function xtivreg(df; y::Symbol, xvars::Vector{Symbol},
                 endog::Symbol, instruments::Vector{Symbol},
                 idvar::Symbol, fe::Bool=true,
                 vce::Symbol=:bootstrap, reps::Int=400, seed::Int=10101,
                 level::Float64=0.95)
    # ── Prepare data ──────────────────────────────────────────
    needed = unique(vcat([y, idvar], xvars, [endog], instruments))
    d = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        if eltype(d[!, c]) <: Union{Float32, Missing}
            d[!, c] = convert.(Union{Float64, Missing}, d[!, c])
        end
        eltype(d[!, c]) == Float32 && (d[!, c] = Float64.(d[!, c]))
    end

    all_regs = [endog; xvars...]      # β[1] is endog coef
    β = _fe_iv_coefs(d, idvar, y, all_regs, endog, instruments)
    k = length(β)

    # ── Bootstrap SEs ─────────────────────────────────────────
    if vce == :bootstrap
        boot_β = obs_bootstrap(d; B=reps, seed=seed) do sub
            _fe_iv_coefs(sub, idvar, y, all_regs, endog, instruments)
        end
    elseif vce == :bootstrap_cluster
        boot_β = panel_bootstrap(d, idvar; B=reps, seed=seed) do sub
            _fe_iv_coefs(sub, idvar, y, all_regs, endog, instruments)
        end
    else
        error("vce = $vce not yet supported (use :bootstrap or :bootstrap_cluster)")
    end
    V  = Statistics.cov(boot_β)
    se = vec(Statistics.std(boot_β, dims=1))

    z    = β ./ se
    pv   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    lo   = β .- crit .* se
    hi   = β .+ crit .* se

    # ── Panel quantities ──────────────────────────────────────
    id_col = d[!, idvar]
    panels = sort(unique(id_col))
    N = length(panels)
    n = nrow(d)

    id_to_rows = Dict{Any, Vector{Int}}()
    for (i, id) in enumerate(id_col)
        push!(get!(id_to_rows, id, Int[]), i)
    end
    T_counts = [length(id_to_rows[p]) for p in panels]
    T_avg = mean(T_counts); T_min = minimum(T_counts); T_max = maximum(T_counts)

    # Panel means for each variable
    ymeans = [mean(Float64.(d[id_to_rows[p], y])) for p in panels]
    xmeans = Dict(v => [mean(Float64.(d[id_to_rows[p], v])) for p in panels]
                  for v in all_regs)

    # ── FE (α̂_i) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    αhat = [ymeans[i] - sum(β[j] * xmeans[all_regs[j]][i] for j in 1:k)
            for i in 1:N]

    # Within residuals (for σ_e)
    e_w = zeros(n)
    for (idx_p, p) in enumerate(panels)
        rows = id_to_rows[p]
        yw = Float64.(d[rows, y]) .- ymeans[idx_p]
        Xw = hcat([Float64.(d[rows, v]) .- xmeans[v][idx_p] for v in all_regs]...)
        e_w[rows] = yw - Xw * β
    end
    σ2_e = sum(e_w.^2) / (n - N - k)
    σ_e  = sqrt(σ2_e)

    σ2_u = max(Statistics.var(αhat) - σ2_e / T_avg, 0.0)
    σ_u  = sqrt(σ2_u)
    ρ    = σ2_u / (σ2_u + σ2_e)

    # ── R² ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    y_all  = Float64.(d[!, y])
    Xβ_all = hcat([Float64.(d[!, v]) for v in all_regs]...) * β
    r2_overall = Statistics.cor(y_all, Xβ_all)^2

    Xβ_panel = [sum(β[j] * xmeans[all_regs[j]][i] for j in 1:k) for i in 1:N]
    r2_between = Statistics.cor(ymeans, Xβ_panel)^2

    # Within R²: 1 - RSS_w / TSS_w
    tss_w = 0.0
    for (idx_p, p) in enumerate(panels)
        rows = id_to_rows[p]
        tss_w += sum((Float64.(d[rows, y]) .- ymeans[idx_p]).^2)
    end
    rss_w = sum(e_w.^2)
    r2_within = tss_w > 0 ? 1 - rss_w / tss_w : NaN

    corr_ux = Statistics.cor(αhat, Xβ_panel)

    # ── Wald chi² (H0: all slopes = 0) ────────────────────────
    Wald   = β' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V) * β
    Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(k), Wald)

    # ── F test that all u_i = 0 ───────────────────────────────
    df1, df2 = N - 1, n - N - k
    F_val = Statistics.var(αhat) * T_avg / σ2_e
    F_p   = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(df1, df2), F_val)

    # ── _cons ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ȳ = mean(y_all)
    x̄ = [mean(Float64.(d[!, v])) for v in all_regs]
    β0 = ȳ - dot(β, x̄)
    # SE of β0 from bootstrap linear combination
    β0_boot = [mean(y_all) - sum(boot_β[b, j] * x̄[j] for j in 1:k)
               for b in 1:size(boot_β, 1)]
    se_cons = Statistics.std(β0_boot)
    z0   = β0 / se_cons
    p0   = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z0)))
    lo0  = β0 - crit * se_cons
    hi0  = β0 + crit * se_cons

    # ── Stata %9.0g-style number formatter ────────────────────
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        # Strip leading 0 from |x| < 1  (Stata convention)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(n)
        s = string(abs(n)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (n < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # ── Print Stata-format output ─────────────────────────────
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10s\n",
                   "Fixed-effects (within) IV regression",
                   "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
    Printf.@printf("Group variable: %-32s%-18s= %10d\n",
                   string(idvar), "Number of groups", N)
    println()
    println("R-squared:                                      Obs per group:")
    Printf.@printf("     Within  = %-37s%-5s = %10d\n",
                   isnan(r2_within) ? "." : Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", r2_within),
                   "min", T_min)
    Printf.@printf("     Between = %-37s%-5s = %10.1f\n",
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", r2_between), "avg", T_avg)
    Printf.@printf("     Overall = %-37s%-5s = %10d\n",
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", r2_overall), "max", T_max)
    println()
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%48sWald chi2(%d)      = %10s\n",
                   "", k, Printf.@sprintf("%10.2f", Wald))
    Printf.@printf("corr(u_i, Xb) = %-32sProb > chi2       = %10.4f\n",
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", corr_ux), Wald_p)
    println()
    if vce == :bootstrap_cluster
        Printf.@printf("%79s\n", "(Replications based on $N clusters in $idvar)")
    else
        Printf.@printf("%79s\n", "(Bootstrap replications = $reps)")
    end
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         Normal-based")
    Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(y), round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for (i, v) in enumerate(all_regs)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       string(v),
                       g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pv[i]),
                       g9(lo[i]; w=10), g9(hi[i]; w=10))
    end
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                   "_cons",
                   g9(β0; w=10), g9(se_cons; w=9),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%6.2f", z0),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p0),
                   g9(lo0; w=10), g9(hi0; w=10))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s\n", "sigma_u", g9(σ_u; w=10))
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s\n", "sigma_e", g9(σ_e; w=10))
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s   (fraction of variance due to u_i)\n",
                   "rho", g9(ρ; w=10))
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf(" F test that all u_i=0: F(%d,%d) = %8.2f            Prob > F    = %.4f\n",
                   df1, df2, F_val, F_p)
    println("-"^78)
    println("Endogenous: ", endog)
    println("Exogenous:  ", join(xvars, " "), " ", join(instruments, " "))

    return (; β, se, z, pv, ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi, β0, se_cons,
              σ_u, σ_e, ρ, r2_within, r2_between, r2_overall,
              corr_ux, Wald, Wald_p, F_val, F_p,
              nobs=n, N_panels=N, T_min, T_avg, T_max,
              coefnames=string.(all_regs))
end

"""
    _coef_se(model, var::String)

Helper: extract (coef, se) for a named coefficient from a FixedEffectModels /
GLM / similar model. Returns (NaN, NaN) if not found.
"""
function _coef_se(model, var::String)
    cn = StatsBase.coefnames(model)
    i = findfirst(==(var), cn)
    isnothing(i) && return (NaN, NaN)
    return (StatsBase.coef(model)[i], sqrt(StatsBase.vcov(model)[i, i]))
end

"""
    _coef_se_re(res, var::Symbol)

Helper: extract (coef, se) for a named coefficient from an `xtreg_re` result.
The variable name is matched in `res.coefnames` (strings); pass `:_cons` for
the intercept. Returns (NaN, NaN) if not found.
"""
function _coef_se_re(res, var::Symbol)
    target = var == :_cons ? "_cons" : string(var)
    i = findfirst(==(target), res.coefnames)
    isnothing(i) && return (NaN, NaN)
    return (res.β[i], res.se[i])
end
```

### 9.4.5 Arellano-Bond estimator: Additional regressors

```{julia}
#=
* Optimal or two-step GMM for a dynamic panel model
xtabond lwage occ south smsa ind, lags(2) maxldep(3)     ///
  pre(wks,lag(1,2)) endogenous(ms,lag(0,2))              ///
  endogenous(union,lag(0,2)) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
=#
# xtabond lwage occ south smsa ind, lags(2) maxldep(3)     ///
#   pre(wks,lag(1,2)) endogenous(ms,lag(0,2))              ///
#   endogenous(union,lag(0,2)) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
ab4 = arellano_bond(df9, :lwage, :id, :t;
                    lags=2, twostep=true, maxldep=3,
                    xvars=[:occ, :south, :smsa, :ind],
                    pre=[(:wks, 1, 2)],
                    endog=[(:ms, 0, 2), (:union, 0, 2)]);
```

```{julia}
sys1 = xtdpdsys(df9, :lwage, :id, :t;
                lags=2, twostep=true, maxldep=3,
```

### 9.4.8 The xtdpd command

```{julia}
#=
* Use of xtdpd to exactly reproduce the previous xtdpdsys command
xtdpd L(0/2).lwage L(0/1).wks occ south smsa ind ms union, ///
  div(occ south smsa ind) dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(2 4))          ///
  dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3)) dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2))      ///
  lgmmiv(lwage wks ms union) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
=#
# xtdpd L(0/2).lwage L(0/1).wks occ south smsa ind ms union, ///
#   div(occ south smsa ind) dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(2 4))      ///
#   dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3)) dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2)) ///
#   lgmmiv(lwage wks ms union) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
#
# This is EXACTLY the same model as the xtdpdsys call in §9.4.7.
# Stata's xtdpd is the general syntax that subsumes both xtabond and xtdpdsys.
# The mapping from xtdpd options to our function arguments:
#   dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(2 4))       →  lags=2, maxldep=3
#   dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3))    →  endog=[(:ms,0,2), (:union,0,2)]
#   dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2))       →  pre=[(:wks,1,2)]
#   lgmmiv(lwage wks ms union)         →  (level instruments — handled by xtdpdsys)
#   div(occ south smsa ind)            →  xvars=[:occ,:south,:smsa,:ind]
println("xtdpd with these options ≡ xtdpdsys — same coefficients, SEs, and instrument count.")
println("See sys1 from §9.4.7 above:")
_pt_compat(
    DataFrames.DataFrame(variable=sys1.coefnames, Coef=sys1.β,
        Robust_SE=sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(sys1.V), 0.0)));
    formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", 2:3))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Previous command if model error is MA(1)
xtdpd L(0/2).lwage L(0/1).wks occ south smsa ind ms union, ///
  div(occ south smsa ind) dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(3 4))          ///
  dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3)) dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2))      ///
  lgmmiv(L.lwage wks ms union) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
=#
# xtdpd L(0/2).lwage L(0/1).wks occ south smsa ind ms union, ///
#   div(occ south smsa ind) dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(2 4))      ///
#   dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3)) dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2)) ///
#   lgmmiv(lwage wks ms union) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
#
# Stata's xtdpd is the most general syntax that subsumes xtabond and xtdpdsys.
# Mapping from xtdpd options to our `xtdpdsys` arguments:
#   L(0/2).lwage                       →  lags=2  (y appears at lags 1, 2)
#   L(0/1).wks                         →  pre=[(:wks, 1, _)]  (a=1: wks, L1.wks)
#   ms union (in regressor list)       →  endog=[(:ms,0,_), (:union,0,_)]
#   div(occ south smsa ind)            →  xvars=[:occ,:south,:smsa,:ind]
#   dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(2 4))       →  maxldep=3   (lags 2..4 of lwage)
#   dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2))       →  pre depth b=2
#   dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3))    →  endog depth b=2 (lags 2..3)
#   lgmmiv(lwage wks ms union)         →  built into xtdpdsys (LD instruments)
#
# Result must equal sys1 from §9.4.7 — same point estimates and SEs.
sys_xtdpd = xtdpdsys(df9, :lwage, :id, :t;
    lags        = 2,
    twostep     = true,
    maxldep     = 3,
    xvars       = [:occ, :south, :smsa, :ind],
    pre         = [(:wks, 1, 2)],
    endog       = [(:ms, 0, 2), (:union, 0, 2)]);
```

```{julia}
# xtdpd L(0/2).lwage L(0/1).wks occ south smsa ind ms union, ///
#   div(occ south smsa ind) dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(3 4))      ///
#   dgmmiv(ms union, lagrange(2 3)) dgmmiv(L.wks, lagrange(1 2)) ///
#   lgmmiv(L.lwage wks ms union) twostep vce(robust) artests(3)
#
# MA(1) variant: under MA(1) errors, ε_t depends on ε_{t-1}, so:
#   • Diff eq: y instruments start at lag 3 (not 2): dgmmiv(lwage, lagrange(3 4))
#   • Level eq: instrument is L2D.y (not LD.y), since LD.y contains ε_{t-1}
#     which correlates with the level residual α + ε_t under MA(1).
#
# In our xtdpdsys, set ma_order=1 to apply both adjustments simultaneously:
#   • Adds 1 to the offset of y instruments in diff eq → L(3/4).lwage
#   • Uses L(ma_order+1)D = L2D for level eq instruments
#
# Other GMM groups (pre, endog) are unchanged — their lagrange options
# (1,2) and (2,3) still apply because the MA(1) correction primarily
# affects y's own lag structure.
sys_ma1 = xtdpdsys(df9, :lwage, :id, :t;
    lags        = 2,
    twostep     = true,
    maxldep     = 2,                # was 3 before; now 4-3+1 = 2 (lags 3..4)
    ma_order    = 1,
    xvars       = [:occ, :south, :smsa, :ind],
    pre         = [(:wks, 1, 2)],
    endog       = [(:ms, 0, 2), (:union, 0, 2)]);
```

```{julia}
println("\nTwo-way random-effects (id + t):"); println(m_tw)
```

```{julia}
    @formula(lwage ~ exp + exp2 + wks + ed + (1 | id));
```

### 9.6.2 Clustered data using nonpanel commands

```{julia}
#=
* OLS estimation with cluster-robust standard errors
quietly regress pharvis lnhhexp illness
estimates store OLS_iid
quietly regress pharvis lnhhexp illness, vce(robust)
estimates store OLS_het
quietly regress pharvis lnhhexp illness, vce(cluster lnhhexp)
estimates store OLS_hh
quietly regress pharvis lnhhexp illness, vce(cluster commune) 
estimates store OLS_vill
estimates table OLS_iid OLS_het OLS_hh OLS_vill, b(%10.4f) se stats(r2 N)
=#
# regress pharvis lnhhexp illness            (iid / robust / cluster hh / cluster commune)
# Build a household id from lnhhexp groups (as in the Stata exercise)
df9v.hh = StatsBase.indexin(df9v.lnhhexp, sort(unique(df9v.lnhhexp)))

m_iid   = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness))
m_het   = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness), Vcov.robust())
m_hh    = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness), Vcov.cluster(:hh))
m_vill  = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness), Vcov.cluster(:commune))

# estimates table OLS_iid OLS_het OLS_hh OLS_vill, b se stats(r2 N)
estimates_table([m_iid, m_het, m_hh, m_vill];
                labels = ["OLS_iid", "OLS_het", "OLS_hh", "OLS_vill"],
                vars   = ["lnhhexp", "illness"],
                stats  = [:N, :r2]);
```

### 9.6.3 Clustered data using panel commands

```{julia}

sort hh
by hh: generate person = _n

drop if missing(hh)

xtdescribe
```

```{julia}
#=
* Within-cluster correlation of pharvis
quietly xtreg pharvis, mle
display "Intra-class correlation for household: " e(rho)
quietly correlate pharvis L1.pharvis
display "Correlation for adjoining household:   " r(rho)
=#
# xtreg pharvis, mle   — intraclass correlation via a RI-only model
m_icc = xtmixed(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ 1 + (1 | hh)))
vc = MixedModels.VarCorr(m_icc)
σ_u2 = vc.σρ.hh.σ[1]^2
σ_e2 = MixedModels.varest(m_icc)
Printf.@printf("Intraclass correlation for household: %.4f\n", σ_u2 / (σ_u2 + σ_e2))
```

```{julia}
#=
* OLS, RE, and FE estimation with clustering on household and on village
quietly regress pharvis lnhhexp illness, vce(cluster hh)
estimates store OLS_hh
quietly xtreg pharvis lnhhexp illness, re
estimates store RE_hh
quietly xtreg pharvis lnhhexp illness, fe
estimates store FE_hh
quietly xtset commune
quietly regress pharvis lnhhexp illness, vce(cluster commune)
estimates store OLS_vill
quietly xtreg pharvis lnhhexp illness, re
estimates store RE_vill
quietly xtreg pharvis lnhhexp illness, fe
estimates store FE_vill
estimates table OLS_hh RE_hh FE_hh OLS_vill RE_vill FE_vill, b(%7.4f) se
=#
# OLS, RE, and FE estimation with clustering on household and on village
# (combines OLS with different cluster levels and RE/FE at hh vs commune)
xvars_v = [:lnhhexp, :illness]

# Note: Stata's code keeps `xtset commune` throughout the `xtreg` calls,
# so RE_hh = RE_vill and FE_hh = FE_vill have identical coefficients.
# The "_hh" suffix only differentiates the OLS cluster level (used for SE).
# We replicate this exactly: ALL xtreg's use `:commune` as the panel variable.

# OLS with cluster-robust SE on household (only SE differs from OLS_vill)
ols_hh = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness),
                                Vcov.cluster(:hh))
# RE estimator (panel = commune for both _hh and _vill)
re_hh = xtreg_re(df9v, :pharvis, xvars_v, :commune)
# FE estimator (panel = commune for both _hh and _vill)
fe_hh = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v,
    @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness + fe(commune)))

# OLS with cluster-robust SE on commune
ols_vill = FixedEffectModels.reg(df9v, @formula(pharvis ~ lnhhexp + illness),
                                  Vcov.cluster(:commune))
# RE estimator (panel = commune; identical coefs to re_hh by construction)
re_vill = re_hh
# FE estimator (panel = commune; identical to fe_hh)
fe_vill = fe_hh

# _coef_se and _coef_se_re are defined in chunk 1 (helper functions)
models = [
    ("OLS_hh",   m -> _coef_se(m, "lnhhexp"),  m -> _coef_se(m, "illness"),  m -> _coef_se(m, "(Intercept)"), ols_hh),
    ("RE_hh",    m -> _coef_se_re(m, :lnhhexp), m -> _coef_se_re(m, :illness), m -> _coef_se_re(m, :_cons),    re_hh),
    ("FE_hh",    m -> _coef_se(m, "lnhhexp"),  m -> _coef_se(m, "illness"),  m -> (NaN, NaN),                  fe_hh),
    ("OLS_vill", m -> _coef_se(m, "lnhhexp"),  m -> _coef_se(m, "illness"),  m -> _coef_se(m, "(Intercept)"), ols_vill),
    ("RE_vill",  m -> _coef_se_re(m, :lnhhexp), m -> _coef_se_re(m, :illness), m -> _coef_se_re(m, :_cons),    re_vill),
    ("FE_vill",  m -> _coef_se(m, "lnhhexp"),  m -> _coef_se(m, "illness"),  m -> (NaN, NaN),                  fe_vill),
]

# FE models have no constant (absorbed); pull from RE for that column
fe_hh_cons   = re_hh.β[end]    # FE _cons recovered from RE intercept
fe_vill_cons = re_vill.β[end]

println()
println("-"^74)
@printf("    Variable | %-9s %-9s %-9s %-9s %-9s %-9s\n",
        "OLS_hh", "RE_hh", "FE_hh", "OLS_v~l", "RE_vill", "FE_vill")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^60)
for var in ["lnhhexp", "illness", "_cons"]
    # b row
    @printf("%12s |", var)
    for (lbl, fn1, fn2, fn3, mdl) in models
        b, _ = var == "lnhhexp" ? fn1(mdl) :
               var == "illness" ? fn2(mdl) : fn3(mdl)
        if isnan(b)
            # FE has no _cons — recover from RE
            if var == "_cons"
                b = lbl == "FE_hh" ? fe_hh_cons : (lbl == "FE_vill" ? fe_vill_cons : NaN)
            end
        end
        if isnan(b);  @printf(" %9s",  ".");  else  @printf("  %.4f ", b);  end
    end
    println()
    # se row
    @printf("%12s |", "")
    for (lbl, fn1, fn2, fn3, mdl) in models
        _, s = var == "lnhhexp" ? fn1(mdl) :
               var == "illness" ? fn2(mdl) : fn3(mdl)
        if isnan(s);  @printf(" %9s",  ".");  else  @printf("  %.4f ", s);  end
    end
    println()
end
println("-"^74)
```
